analysis.title: 2026 Midterm Election Series – September 30, 2026
key_insights: Trump's approval has fallen to 37% in a WSJ poll as of Sep 28, the lowest for a president entering a midterm since 1990. This has widened the Senate map. Democrats are now favored to win both chambers.

Odds of Democrats winning both the House and the Senate rose to ~62% from ~52% two weeks earlier (Bloomberg/Kalshi). Other combinations: Dem House/GOP Senate 29%, GOP House/Dem Senate 1.4%, GOP House/GOP Senate 8% (data as of 9/29/2026).

Nine Senate races are toss-ups: Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Nebraska, Ohio and Texas. Democrats need to win 5 for outright control, possibly 6 given uncertainty over Sen. Fetterman's role in the next Congress. Democrats lead in betting markets and polls in Alaska, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas. Republicans lead in Iowa, Kansas and Nebraska.

Georgia, New Hampshire and North Carolina are no longer treated as battlegrounds because Democratic leads are large enough. The GOP is spending time and money in reliably red states (Alabama, Oklahoma, Texas), which erodes its cash advantage.

Market Intelligence expects no material policy or market impact from a change of control, since Democrats would not reach the 2/3 needed in both chambers to override vetoes. It expects gridlock like the last two years of Biden, Trump 1.0 and Obama, and says markets typically react favorably to gridlock. It would not adjust portfolios for a Blue Wave and would buy any dip around the election.

A Democratic House would control funding and have investigative powers. It could try to end the US/Iran conflict by pulling funding or suing over the 90-day war-powers limit. Impeachment is possible but unlikely to reach the 66 Senate votes needed to remove Trump. Budget fights could cause short government shutdowns, which JPM says historically create buy-the-dip opportunities.

A Democratic Senate would control confirmations of cabinet members and judges, which could push Trump toward centrist nominees. With both chambers, Democrats would have more control over budget negotiations and would pass bills to put Republicans on record for 2028.

Affordability is the dominant campaign theme. 42% of voters trust Democrats more on the economy versus 34% for Republicans (NPR). Pew lists the economy as the top voting issue at 29%, of which cost of living is 15%.

The Fed's watchdog found no criminal violations in the renovation project Trump had used to target Powell. It is unclear whether this affects Powell's decision to step down, and the timing would depend on a possible change in Senate control and the confirmation path for a Trump nominee.

The Supreme Court ruled against Trump's effort to restrict mail-in voting and is allowing use of federal voter eligibility databases (DHS SAVE). About one-third of 2024 voters used mail ballots (Dem ~37%, GOP ~24%).

Ambassador David Perdue said Trump offered to sell weapons to China during Xi's US visit, which Trump denies. Trump has not approved a $14bn Taiwan weapons package. JPM flags that anything seen as friendly to China risks lowering Republican turnout.
House: Cook Political Report sees Democrats likely to win 197 seats and the GOP 195, with 11 Lean D, 10 Lean R and 21 toss-ups (16 held by Republicans). 218 are needed for control.
Fundraising: Democratic Senate candidates have raised ~$585.2mm versus $336.9mm for Republicans. In the House, Democrats have raised ~$1,009.5mm versus $814.9mm (FEC).

JPM Delta One offers election baskets and pairs: a beta-neutral Democratic pair (JP9DEMP, long JP9DEML/short JP9DEMS) and Republican pair (JP9REPP), built from Polymarket odds and an Election Score across ~3,000 US stocks. JPM says JP9DEMP's performance is largely idiosyncratic, with limited explanatory power from traditional risk factors.

Joyce Chang (7/16 note): Iran-war and gas prices, which remain 31% above pre-conflict levels, have hurt Trump's economic ratings. She expects the House to flip with a margin short of a full blue wave (Democratic majority of 220-230 seats), because redistricting left only 20-30 competitive seats versus ~90 in past cycles. Her note says Republicans remain favored to retain the Senate, which conflicts with the current betting-market view.

Dubravko (6/24 note): the president's party has lost ~27 House and ~3 Senate seats on average over 23 midterms since 1934. Gridlock has coincided with higher S&P 500 returns since 1950 (+20% vs +18% on election-date basis; +25% vs +18% from start of new Congress).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher gas prices from the Iran conflict have hurt Trump's economic approval, and affordability is the main midterm issue.

trade_ideas.description: Buy any market dip around the midterm election, including a Blue Wave scenario
trade_ideas.rationale: Divided government would produce gridlock, which JPM says markets typically react to favorably, and no 2/3 majority exists to override vetoes.

trade_ideas.description: JPM Delta One Democratic pair JP9DEMP (long JP9DEML, short JP9DEMS) and Republican pair JP9REPP (long JP9REPL, short JP9REPS) to trade or hedge election-odds moves
trade_ideas.rationale: Beta-neutral pairs built from Polymarket odds isolate idiosyncratic election-driven moves and hedge election uncertainty.

trade_ideas.description: Buy the dip around short-term government shutdowns caused by budget fights under a Democratic House
trade_ideas.rationale: Shutdowns have historically created buy-the-dip opportunities.

risk_factors: Election security and integrity concerns, including the hiring of attorney David Levin, who pled guilty to election interference, and military involvement in election cybersecurity
Voter intimidation: 52% of adults are concerned about it at polling sites and 67% about political pressure in elections (Gallup)
Possible impeachment proceedings and budget fights leading to short shutdowns under a Democratic House
Uncertainty over the Fed chair's timing and the Senate confirmation path if Senate control changes
Trade tension with Canada and the Iran conflict weighing on the economy and Republican prospects
vol_and_positioning: JPM Delta One uses Polymarket odds to build beta-neutral long/short election pairs (JP9DEMP and JP9REPP) that isolate idiosyncratic moves and can hedge election exposure.
geopolitical: US/Iran conflict: a Democratic House could end it by pulling funding or by suing over the 90-day congressional approval requirement
A War Powers Resolution passed with some Republican votes, demanding Trump seek congressional authorization for the Iran war or end military action
Trump has not approved a $14bn weapons package earmarked for Taiwan, and the US ambassador's claim that Trump offered to sell weapons to China is disputed
US and China cut tariffs on basic goods but left rare earths out
Trump's trade actions against Canada, including beef, add to GOP worries in border states. Canada is the top trading partner for Iowa, Maine, North Carolina and Ohio.

tension_points.bull_case: Betting markets give Democrats about a 62% chance of taking both chambers. Trump's approval is at a record low of 37%, and Democrats lead in five of the nine toss-up Senate races.
tension_points.bear_case: Joyce Chang's July note says Republicans remain favored to keep the Senate and that the House margin will fall short of a full blue wave because redistricting cut competitive seats to 20-30. Iowa, Kansas and Nebraska still lean GOP.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Democrats failing to win 5 of the 9 toss-up Senate races (6 if Fetterman's role is uncertain).

theme_stances.key_argument: Democratic control without a 2/3 majority produces gridlock, which markets typically treat favorably, so dips around the election are buyable.
theme_stances.evidence: Any dip creating around the election, we would be buyers.
